newsitem.title: USA: Russian reporters freed in Chechnya soon: media mogul.
newsitem.headline: Russian reporters freed in Chechnya soon: media mogul.

text.p: Russian journalists taken hostage in the breakaway Chechnya region could be freed soon, a Russian entrepreneur and media tycoon said on Tuesday.

Vladimir Goussinsky, head of the Most Group conglomerate, which includes the NTV television network, told reporters he had met regularly with senior Chechen officials about the kidnapping of NTV reporter Elena Masyuk and her two-man crew.

"We are aware of what is being done by the Chechen government in order to find the reporters," he said. "We think that whatever it is they are trying to do should come to fruition in the very near future."

Masyuk, one of Russia's best-known reporters, and her colleagues were kidnapped last month about 30 miles (45 km) west of the capital, Grozny. A reporter and cameraman from the Vzglyad programme also were seized last week in Grozny.
The kidnappings have strained the atmosphere between Russia and Chechnya. Goussinsky suggested the hostage-takings could be aimed at sabotaging peace negotiations between Russia and Chechnya.
"I think the motivation is complex. I think the kidnappers are from the criminal world (and) ... are carrying out a political order," he said, speaking through an interpreter.
Chechnya was devastated by Russia's ill-fated 1994-96 military effort to crush its independence campaign.

Goussinsky, who was in New York on business, received copies of more than a dozen letters sent to Russian and Chechen officials by human rights and journalist watchdog groups expressing concern about the NTV crew's kidnapping.

The groups included the United States' Carter Centre, Human Rights Watch/Helsinki, the Committee to Protect Journalists, the Canadian Committee to Protect Journalists and Princeton University's Kennan Institute for Advanced Russian Studies.
